label: Salt-bridge dissociation, guidance recovery vs adjacent-window covered length, K15 base, horizons 1/5/10/30/50/90 ns
series: L2 (revision of L: window placed immediately before the origin frame 10, E01 Protocol A)

length_definition.unit: covered length (ns); frame count same as L01/L02, but the window is the last L/0.1+1 frames ending at the origin frame 10
length_definition.note: Length 0 = frame 10 only; 0.1 ns = frames 9-10; ...; 1.0 ns = frames 0-10 (identical to the L condition, used for the premise check). In L the window was frames 0..(L/0.1) paired with origin frame 10, leaving a time gap for short lengths.

base.name: K15 base for salt-bridge dissociation: train 58 / test 30 proteins, static 5 features, HistGBM (120 iters, lr 0.075, 31 leaves, min_samples_leaf 15, L2 0.02, seed 42) retrained per condition; full_history = static + 6 history statistics (first, mean, std, min, last-first, fraction <= 4.0 A). Salt-bridge candidates: charged heavy-atom minimum distance, origin <= 4.0 A (bound pair), label > 4.0 A, sequence separation >= 2.

bootstrap_note: Within each resample, static-only, full-history and adjacent-mean AUPRCs are recomputed and the gain and recovery are recomputed inside the sample. Models are not refit; per-candidate predicted probabilities are resampled. Pooled AUPRC uses a numpy implementation of sklearn's average_precision_score (threshold-grouped), verified against sklearn to <1e-9 on the full test set for every condition and horizon. Macro AUPRC within a resample is the multiplicity-weighted mean of per-protein AUPRCs over proteins whose AUPRC is defined. Draws whose resampled gain is not positive are excluded from the interval (counted in n_draws_with_nonpositive_gain), as in L33. Note: with 30 test proteins the intervals are coarser than on the strong base (100 proteins).
